svg.aria-label: The visibility harness on the settlement-ingest-3 worker's stop flag. Left panel: a plain, non-volatile stop field never exits its spin loop; PrintCompilation shows C2 recompiling SettlementLoop::run and hoisting the load of stop out before the loop so the writer's store is never re-read, and the observed run is killed manually after ten minutes still spinning in the billions. Right panel: the same loop with stop declared volatile reloads the field every iteration and exits within roughly one scheduling quantum of the writer's store, because volatile forbids the JIT from hoisting the load and installs a happens-before edge between the write and the next read.
svg.text: D-209 — The visibility harness: non-volatile stop flag vs. volatile
Non-volatile flag — settlement-ingest-3 never sees the write
boolean stop = false; // plain field
while (!stop) { spins++; }
-XX:+PrintCompilation (after ~10k loops):
234 57 4 SettlementLoop::run (12 bytes)
235 57 made not entrant
235 61 4 SettlementLoop::run (12 bytes)
(C2 compile — loop body hoisted out)
C2's hoisted form (pseudo-asm, read top to bottom):
MOV R8, [stop] ; read ONCE before loop
TEST R8, R8
JNZ L_exit ; if stop!=0, skip loop entirely
L_loop:
INC [spins] ; no reload of [stop] in the body
JMP L_loop ; unconditional — infinite
L_exit:
Reading it: the load of stop happens once, before L_loop. The
writer's later store to stop has no thread-visible effect — no
happens-before edge exists to force a re-read. Elapsed: never exits
(observed run: killed manually after 10 min, spins in the billions).
add
volatile
volatile flag — exits promptly
volatile boolean stop = false;
while (!stop) { spins++; }
C2's form with the volatile read:
L_loop:
MOV R8, [stop] ; VOLATILE — reloaded every iteration
TEST R8, R8
JNZ L_exit
INC [spins]
JMP L_loop
L_exit:
; x86-64 TSO needs no fence for a plain load;
; the JIT is forbidden from hoisting/caching it
Reading it: JIT cannot prove [stop] is loop-invariant once the
field is volatile, so the load stays inside L_loop. The writer's
store becomes visible on the next iteration's reload.
Observed run: exits within one scheduling quantum of the writer's
store — order-of-magnitude low tens of milliseconds on x86-64 and
aarch64 alike (both give volatile the same happens-before guarantee).
Elapsed time, side by side (order-of-magnitude, not measured absolutes)
non-volatile stop: loop runs until the process is killed — no upper bound observed
volatile stop: loop exits within roughly one scheduling quantum after the write
This is the store-buffer / invalidate-queue reality, not a "flush to main memory" event:
MESI already keeps caches coherent across cores. What volatile changes is compiler
licence — it forbids hoisting the load and inserts the happens-before edge (JLS 17.4.5)
between the writer's store and the reader's next load, so the reader is guaranteed to
observe SOME later value of stop, not pinned to a stale register-cached copy.
